title: Keeping a self-checkout moving
target: How to treat the self-service till in Supermarket Simulator as a checkout with conditions of its own, so it keeps serving customers instead of stalling.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A self-service till placed in the shop
At least one other lane customers can use
The scanning side already set up

steps.do: Expect conditions rather than a smaller version of a staffed lane.
steps.because: the game checks whether the machine can be used at all before it takes a customer (AutomatedCheckout, CanSelfCheckoutUsable)

steps.do: Watch for a customer who wants help, not only for a machine that has stopped.
steps.because: wanting help is tracked as its own question, apart from whether the machine works (IsSelfCheckoutWantHelp)

steps.do: Check that somebody is actually standing in front of it before you expect anything to happen.
steps.because: the game keeps track of whether a customer is at the till (HasCheckoutCustomer)

steps.do: Keep it where you can watch it, because the shop decides how much of it to draw.
steps.because: a renderer switches its detail by distance (LODCheckoutRenderer)

steps.do: Count it as one of your checkout kinds when you plan the front of the shop.
steps.because: a checkout carries a type and the automated machine is one of those types rather than a system apart (CheckoutType)

steps.do: Use the same scanning habits at it as at any other till.
steps.because: the scanning side is shared, so what differs is the rules around the machine rather than the act of scanning (ScanAnimationHandler)

commonMistakes: Treating a self-checkout as a smaller staffed lane and expecting the same customers to use it.
Waiting for the machine to fail instead of watching for a customer who wants a hand.
Blaming the machine when nobody is standing in front of it.
Placing it out of sight and then wondering why it stalls.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
